title: Autonomous stabilization of many-body entanglement with Floquet Hamiltonians and weak measurement
abstract: Reaching a technological advantage with large quantum systems requires safeguarding their many-body entanglement. Dissipation typically acts to decohere a quantum system via random projective noise but, when judiciously engineered together with coherent interactions, it can funnel the system towards a target entangled state. The native interactions and dissipative channels available to most systems are, however, difficult to combine effectively. Here we propose interleaving Floquet Hamiltonian engineering, which allows the construction of non-native coherent interactions, with weak measurement, which enables a tuneable dissipative channel, to enable programmable and autonomous stabilization of many-body entanglement. We show this analytically and numerically for the central-spin system of a semiconductor quantum dot, for which we construct spin-squeezed and Schrödinger-cat states that are stabilized against realistic levels of dephasing. Our approach is applicable to any system compatible with periodic drives and tuneable measurement strength and could enable novel approaches to practical error correction.
summary: This paper proposes a novel technique to autonomously stabilize complex many-body entangled states, such as spin-squeezed and Schrödinger-cat states, in quantum systems. The technique combines periodic Hamiltonian engineering (Floquet drives) with weak measurement to create a programmable dissipative environment. This approach offers a powerful pathway for practical quantum computation by actively counteracting environmental decoherence.
main_problem: Safeguarding many-body entanglement in large quantum systems against decoherence caused by dissipation.
main_result: The authors successfully demonstrated an autonomous protocol to stabilize both spin-squeezed and collective Schrödinger-cat states, even against realistic noise levels.
method: The method interleaves Floquet Hamiltonian engineering to create non-native coherent interactions with weak measurement to impose a tunable dissipative channel.
model_or_system: The system is modeled using a central-spin system in a semiconductor quantum dot, coupling an electron spin ($\vec{S}$) to a nuclear spin ensemble ($\vec{I}$). The dynamics are governed by a stroboscopic evolution mimicking a Lindblad master equation.
key_observables: Squeezing parameter ($\xi_2^R$), Cat infidelity ($1-F$), and the steady-state density matrix ($ho_{ss}$).
important_parameters: Weak measurement strength ($\epsilon$), Liouvillian gap ($\Delta$), and the ratio of coupling strengths ($\Omega_+/\Omega_-$).
main_assumptions: The process assumes the ability to separate coherent and dissipative steps in time, and that the auxiliary system decay is fast enough for adiabatic elimination.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the dissipative engineering cycle, show Wigner snapshots of stabilized states (squeezed/cat), and plot time evolution of the squeezing parameter and cat infidelity, demonstrating stabilization below the Standard Quantum Limit (SQL).
paper_structure: The paper details the theoretical framework by combining Floquet engineering and weak measurement into a stroboscopic cycle. It then applies this to the quantum dot model to derive effective master equations for specific entangled states, analyzing robustness against various noise sources.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, platform-agnostic blueprint for actively controlling quantum dynamics using engineered dissipation, which is a key concept in quantum error correction and quantum control.
